text:
Matt Coronato's overtime winner against the Flyers on Nov. 8 capped a comeback and got him the headlines, but his season so far reads differently from the one Calgary was hoping for. He has 15 points in 19 games, 11 of them assists, and only four goals on 4.05 expected (the quality of his chances), so the finishing is right on what the chances deserve. The chances themselves are thin: 1.7 expected goals over his last ten, below what we'd expect for his minutes.

The bigger worry is five on five. Calgary has had just 42.7% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly seven points worse than without him, and his team has scored 3.9 more goals than its chances deserved while he's out there. Evolving-Hockey had a similar warning last season: opponents generated more with him on the ice than against almost any other forward.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says the tools are real: 98th percentile among forwards for slot chances last season. The question is whether the Flames can keep the puck at the right end long enough to use them.
headline: Coronato: assists up, goals and defense down
